text: {"score":3,"justification":"Numbers match the card and tool outputs, and the cautious 'inconclusive' leaning fits the hybrid_review result (undecided). But the summary contradicts itself and offers thin guidance. The headline says '30 of 30 charts support the billed level' while the next step says the records are 'too thin to judge', yet the exchange returned 30 of 30 usable charts. The 'claims pattern is concerning, but chart evidence does not support upcoding' line is stronger than the evidence allows, given that only 12 of the 99215 claims were documented. The headline 'high in every complexity group' is loosely true, but it does not mention the strongest signal (23% of 99215 claims at 0 conditions vs 1.8% overall). The cited examples are only two low-complexity claims; no high-complexity contrast and no supported-99215 examples (e.g., C0109089, with 0 conditions but documented high MDM at 32 min) are given, though that claim is the most relevant to reconciling claims vs charts. The rationale repeats itself (z_adj 10.0, 0 of 30 charts, 2 of 21 stated twice). Next steps are generic, with no specific claims to request and no mention of the missing data (minutes not recorded). An investigator would have to redo some of the analysis.","problems":["Headline asserts '30 of 30 charts support the billed level' while the next step says records are 'too thin to judge' — internally inconsistent","Only 12 of 99215 claims were documented, yet the summary says chart evidence 'does not support upcoding' — overreaches","Redundant repeated figures (z_adj 10.0, 0 of 30, 2 of 21 appear twice) and an unexplained 'z_adj' label","Only two cited examples, both low-complexity; omits C0109089 (0 conditions but documented high MDM) which is key to reconciling claims vs charts","Next steps are generic: no specific claim IDs, no mention of missing time documentation or the 2 notes with data review but no tests","Does not highlight the 0-condition 99215 rate (23.1% vs 1.8% overall) as the sharpest signal"]}
